title: God speaks as to friends (Dei Verbum 2)
hookLine: God speaks to people as friends and lives among them
tomorrow: why does the priest kiss the book at Mass?

lines: FRIENDS TALK MORE THAN ONE WAY.
cards: The voice memo, the long careful text, the two-word reply: friends talk more than one way.
When the bishops of the Second Vatican Council set out to explain how God makes himself known, they could have reached for a courtroom, a classroom or a rulebook.
In paragraph two of Dei Verbum they reached for friendship. The invisible God, they write, speaks to people as friends.
Which leaves a question people still argue about at the kitchen table: if God talks like a friend, how should anyone talk back?

teach.b: First, the paragraph. Dei Verbum 2 says God speaks out of the abundance of his love, to invite people into fellowship with himself. The picture isn't new.
Exodus says the Lord spoke to Moses face to face, the way someone speaks to a friend, and in John's Gospel Jesus says, "But I have called you friends."

God speaks through deeds and words bound together, the council adds, and Christ is the fullness of it: God speaks as to friends, and lives among them. Second, one answer: plainly. Friends don't read each other scripts.

Say what happened today, in your own words, and leave room to listen. Teresa of Avila, earlier on this path, described prayer as a friendly conversation with the one who loves us. Third, the other answer: in shared words.
Old friends have sayings worn smooth with use. When the disciples asked Jesus how to pray, he gave them words, the Our Father.
The rosary, the psalms and the prayers of the Mass are words the Church keeps saying together, and on the day your own words run out, they're still there.
Fourth, where that leaves a person.
The council's paragraph doesn't pick between them.
Some people pray both ways before breakfast.

how: Catholics pray both in their own words and with set prayers such as the Our Father and the rosary; Dei Verbum 2 is often read in classes on revelation and in preparing adults for baptism.

games.q: what does “god speaks as to friends” mean?
o: God speaking only to close friends of the saints
God answering prayers only from the Church's friends
God revealing himself like a friend speaking, not a rulebook

games.q: friends, in the paragraph and behind it — tap the pairs.
p: face to face, as with a friend

s: Dei Verbum pictures revelation as a rulebook handed down
it pictures friendship: God speaks to people as friends and lives among them.
the friendship picture was in the Bible long before the council
Moses face to face, as with a friend; and Jesus: I have called you friends.
praying with set words means you're not really talking to God
when the disciples asked how to pray, Jesus gave them words.

games.q: your friend says memorized prayers are fake, like reading a script to someone you love. what's the strongest case for the other side?
o: old friends share words, and Jesus himself gave the Our Father.
memorized prayers are faster, so they fit a busy day better.
God only listens to official words the Church has approved.
games.why: when the disciples asked how to pray, Jesus gave them words. shared words can be friendship too, especially when your own run out.

practice: Close your eyes and sit the way you'd sit across from a good friend, unhurried. If you pray, say one real thing about today to God in plain words, then leave the rest of the quiet for listening.
If you don't, simply notice what it's like to be spoken to as a friend, not a stranger.

wordCard.voice: God speaks as to friends. Dei Verbum's picture of revelation: an invitation into friendship, in deeds and words, made full in Christ. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin in Dei Verbum 2: God addresses people as friends.

carryVoice: One line to keep: as friends, which is how the council says God speaks, and lives among people. See you tomorrow.
